about: The incident timeline as data, made from timeline.md by team/incidents/tools/timeline.mjs (never edit by hand; edit timeline.md). See README.md.

items.label: evidence
items.text: IPMA expects the storm earlier, Wednesday morning; Lisbon among the hardest hit; avoid unnecessary travel (Lusa)

items.label: fact
items.text: The government declares an alert situation for the mainland on Wednesday, 00:00 to 23:59: schools and non-essential public services close; outdoor events suspended

sources.label: portugal.gov.pt (page dated 12:10; S41 updated with it at 17:27), read by weather@

items.label: evidence
items.text: Web Summit's organisers following the alerts with ANEPC and PSP; no sign yet of cancelling Wednesday

items.label: evidence
items.text: Lisbon's mayor: "Tudo indica que a Web Summit não poderá funcionar amanhã"; the decision is the Interior Ministry's and the organisers'

items.label: fact
items.text: IPMA red warning for wind, Lisbon district, Wednesday 12:00 to 21:00 (first read by the newsroom)

items.label: evidence
items.text: Web Summit in doubt; Tagus bridges limited to 60 km/h; Lisbon tunnels closed from midnight; Metro keeps running

items.label: evidence
items.text: the storm leaves Web Summit with a thin audience

items.label: fact
items.text: Dinis: the storm is our case study (a dynamic team, the decision graph)

items.label: evidence
items.text: water enters a pavilion between halls 4 and 5; participants leave early

items.label: fact
items.text: IPMA raises Lisbon's rain warning to red, Wednesday 12:00 to 18:00

sources.label: IPMA open data, read by weather@

items.label: fact
items.text: Web Summit: no change to Wednesday's programme announced on its homepage or news page

items.label: evidence
items.text: the government recommends suspending Web Summit on Wednesday; the decision rests with the organisers

items.label: evidence
items.text: (unofficial) an attendee post says the event is "most likely" closed tomorrow; speculation, not an announcement

items.label: evidence
items.text: no organiser statement after the government's recommendation (the live blog's last update read)

items.label: fact
items.text: Incident declared (P1, run on account A) at Dinis's word

items.label: fact
items.text: Vicky's weather desk full check: IPMA's two red warnings for Lisbon unchanged since 17:42 (wind 12:00 to 21:00, rain 12:00 to 18:00); no Web Summit change

items.label: evidence
items.text: Organisers checked again: no decision on Wednesday; their last line is still "assessing with ANEPC and PSP"

items.label: fact
items.text: Lead handed over: incident.conductor@web-summit.dinis takes the lead of WS-214 from conductor@web-summit.dinis, at Dinis's word (team/incidents/BRIEF.md); the timeline is kept newest first from here

items.label: fact
items.text: No Web Summit decision on Wednesday found (organiser channels readable without a login)

items.label: fact
items.text: No Web Summit decision on Wednesday: websummit.com (home, /news/, sitemap), its official Bluesky (last post 17:36, "wrap on Day 1") and Jornal de Negócios live (last entry 18:24)

items.label: fact
items.text: analysis (incident.meteorologist@, labelled): worst window Wed 12:00 to 18:00, peak most likely ~15:00 to 19:00 around the wind's swing to north-west, easing but dangerous to 21:00; red wind was known ~27.5 h ahead; confidence medium on the window, low on the peak

sources.label: data/weather/analysis.md (from IPMA warnings, communiqué no. 2, LPPT TAF, IPMA model, read 19:01)
